bib.title: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI

read.skipped: Case-study figures (Appendix C, about chars 99000-252700, 100+ GPT-4V examples) and per-discipline Tables 5-10 were skimmed, not read line by line; they are qualitative examples and subject-level repeats of Table 4.

question: Can a college-level, multi-discipline, multimodal benchmark measure expert-level perception, knowledge and reasoning in large multimodal models?
hypothesis: Existing multimodal benchmarks test commonsense and basic perception, so a benchmark needing college-level knowledge and reasoning will expose a large gap between current models and human experts.
contributions: MMMU: 11.5K college-level multimodal questions across 6 disciplines, 30 subjects, 183 subfields, 30 image types, with interleaved text and images
Evaluation of 28 open-source LMMs plus GPT-4V and Gemini, text-only and OCR/caption baselines, and human experts

method.summary: Annotators (50+ college students) collected 13K questions from textbooks, quizzes and exams, deduplicated and cleaned them to 11.5K, and split into dev/validation/test. Models are evaluated zero-shot with micro-averaged accuracy using rule-based answer extraction.
method.task: multimodal multiple-choice and short open-ended question answering

datasets.name: MMMU
datasets.source: college exams, quizzes, textbooks and lecture materials; annotators avoided sources prohibiting copying/redistribution
datasets.preprocessing: lexical overlap and source URL similarity to find duplicates, author review, format/typo check, difficulty labelling in 4 levels, about 10% very easy removed

models.name: 28 open-source LMMs (e.g. LLaVA-1.5, BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, Qwen-VL, CogVLM, Fuyu-8B, OpenFlamingo, Kosmos2, mPLUG-Owl2)

other.note: several of these numbers come from vendor reports, not authors' runs

models.name: Text-only LLMs: GPT-4, Llama2-7B, FLAN-T5-XXL, Vicuna-13B

inference.prompting: zero-shot; each model's default prompt for MC or open QA if available, otherwise prompt engineering on the validation set and the best prompt used; few-shot (1/3/5 shot from dev set) only for OpenFlamingo and Otter

other.answer_extraction: regex for numbers and conclusion phrases; invalid MC answer replaced by random option; invalid open answer counted wrong

metrics.name: micro-averaged accuracy
metrics.definition: correct / total over all questions, MC and open, via rule-based matching

baselines: Frequent Choice (most frequent option per subject in validation)
eval.protocol: validation (900) and test (10,500, via EvalAI leaderboard); humans: 90 seniors, 3 per subject, 30 questions each, textbooks allowed, no internet; no seeds, runs or significance tests stated

limits: Authors concede manual curation may carry biases and college-level subjects are not sufficient to test Expert AGI.
No mapping from MMMU score to 90th percentile of skilled adults is established.
Many leaderboard entries (starred) are author-provided outputs, not run by the MMMU team; prompts differ per model (default prompt or tuned on validation).
Human expert baseline uses 90 students on validation only, textbooks allowed; no test-set human score.
Error analysis covers 150 GPT-4V errors only; no error analysis for other models.
Answer extraction is rule-based regex; unparseable multiple-choice responses get a random guess, which inflates low scores toward chance.

Benchmark is English-only and image-required; public test labels are not released (test via EvalAI), but contamination is addressed only by annotator selection of questions with answers not readily available.
Scores dated: top is GPT-4o 69.1 val at v4 (June 2024); later models have exceeded this (not in paper).
